messages:
ops-incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: Detected spike in 5xx for customer PioneerHealth (vpc-pioneer-edge) — autoscale unaffected. Root cause suspected: NLB health check failures causing targets to be drained. Paging @oncall-amber.
oncall-amber: Acked. Pulling logs now. Any impact window or is this ongoing?
sanjeev: seeing 502 spikes from ingress NLB to tenant pool. 5xx rate ~ 12% for last 3m. Origin appears to be tenant egress to upstream billing API (outbound). Healthchecks show intermittent 504 from target.
marta: Confirmed from NLB metrics: target unhealthy count increased from 0 to 3/6 over 10m. Health check latency spikes to 10-15s before timeouts.
nick: Checking security group flow logs for egress drops. Running query on VPC flow logs...
emma: Other customers on same private deployment? I see dedicated pool "pioneer-ded-3" isolated; no other tenant should be sharing.
jess: Customer reported errors in app logs: "upstream read timeout" and retries escalate to 502. They've opened a Zendesk but want quick mitigation.
kamal: Hypothesis: upstream provider is rate-limiting health-check IP due to probe frequency causing probe throttling -> NLB marks targets unhealthy. Could be egress firewall or WAF back-pressure.
oncall-amber: Quick mitigation options: 1) reduce healthcheck frequency on NLB temporarily 2) re-route egress via alternate TGW to bypass upstream rate limiter 3) add retry/backoff on app (control plane). Which is fastest?
sanjeev: Option 1 is fastest. We can adjust target group health check interval from 10s to 30s with immediate effect. Doing change now in staging then prod? Need approval.
marta: Make change in prod TG only after coordination. Also adjust health check path to a lighter probe ("/ping") rather than full upstream call.
nick: SG logs show no DENY for outbound to upstream IPs. But I do see SYN retransmits and RSTs from upstream addresses. Suggests upstream closing.
emma: I'm going to open a quick runbook entry: /runbooks/vpc/nlb-healthcheck-flap.md (draft) — link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/nlb-flap
ops-incident-bot: NOTE: Incident severity elevated to S2 due to customer visible errors and no ETA.
jess: I'll update customer Slack with "we're aware, performing mitigation steps, ETA ~15m". Ping PioneerAccount to expect transient 502s.
kamal: prepping Terraform change for healthcheck interval; will push canary to one TG first. Command snippet:
```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:... --health-check-interval-seconds 30 --health-check-path /ping
```
sanjeev: Rolling to target-group pioneer-ded-3-tg-a now. Monitor metrics.
marta: metrics look better on TG-A: unhealthy_count drops to 1 and latency down to 200ms. Keep rolling.
nick: Also enabling short-lived egress route to natgw-bak in same region as temp bypass: adding route table entry to send Pioneer tenant CIDR -> natgw-bak. Will coordinate with infra.
oncall-amber: Please record the exact commands and approval in PR.
emma: PR created: https://git.redwood/pr/4302 — contains healthcheck change and route update as reversible changes.
jess: Pioneer support updated: "Thanks, we'll monitor".
kamal: After TG roll and route change, 5xx rate down to 1.2% — still above baseline but improving. Keeping session stickiness and no drain.
sanjeev: Observed TTLs on customer DNS low (10s) — could spike traffic on re-resolution. Noted.
marta: Monitoring for 30m. If stable we revert route change and keep healthcheck interval at 15s instead of 10s as a compromise.
ops-incident-bot: Reminder: handoff in 25m to next oncall (nick). Prepare notes.
oncall-amber: I'm stepping out in 20m. Nick will take over. Nick please ack when you see handoff.
nick: Ack. I'll watch metrics and coordinate with Pioneer SRE if anything regresses.
emma: Creating follow-up action items: postmortem if root cause confirmed as upstream rate-limiting; propose permanent mitigations: healthcheck redesign, pinned egress IP, or provider coordination.
jess: Customer impact summary for postmortem: PioneerHealth reported increased 502s starting 04:03 UTC, peak 04:10–04:22 UTC, affecting ~2% of their requests, degraded user experience for 10 minutes. No data exfiltration.
kamal: Leaving note: reverted route by 04:50 UTC after stability. Kept healthcheck at 15s. Documented commands in PR.
sanjeev: Closing loop with monitoring: set alert threshold lower to detect future probe throttling earlier: add synthetic probe with geo-dispersed checks.
marta: Handing off runbook ownership to Nick. Nick, please own follow-up and coordinate with Customer Success for any credits.
nick: Will do. I'll open a follow-up ticket and schedule a 1-hour review with Pioneer SRE next week.
oncall-amber: Thanks team. Moving to resolved state pending postmortem. :white_check_mark: 
ops-incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: initial mitigation succeeded, follow-ups scheduled. Incident duration ~00:50. Generated incident ID I-2026-1771239999."
